text: Execution plans and DMVs show you a query right now. Query Store persists query text, every plan, and runtime stats to disk, across restarts -- something DMVs like sys.dm_exec_query_stats never survive.

Azure SQL Database has this on by default; on-prem you turn it on per database. This is the Plan Summary view for one query -- two clusters of dots at very different heights means this query ran under two meaningfully different plans.

Top Resource Consumers ranks the top twenty-five queries by whichever metric you pick -- duration, CPU time, logical reads. This replaces guessing which query to tune first with an actual measured ranking.
Query text, every plan a query has used, and runtime stats per plan, all persisted to disk. Capture mode set to automatic skips one-off ad hoc queries so the store doesn't fill with noise.
Reading a single query's plan history and knowing which queries are worth looking at -- that's the foundation. Next up: catching a query that regressed, and forcing a fix.
